title: vmsacars flight thresholds
description: A sparse flight-thresholds layer document (version 2). The full set of values lives in the client; every document lists only what it changes, grouped by flight phase (PirepState names, with goAround and circuit under phases) and feature. Used for the published artifacts/settings.json (the aircraft-class overrides, built from src/settings/overrides/*.json[c]) and for an airline's settings/flight.json[c] in its config zip. values applies to every aircraft; each override layers its values on top when its selector matches (class overrides first, then icao overrides, each in file order). The client applies, last one winning: its compiled-in defaults, the Replane flight namespace, this artifact, then the airline file.

version.description: Document format version. The client accepts only 2 (grouped keys); version 1 (flat keys) never shipped.

override.description: One override document. Needs at least one selector; values uses the same groups as defaults and lists only the keys it changes.

icao.description: ICAO aircraft type designators this override applies to, matched case-insensitively.

class.description: Aircraft class this override applies to. A general-aviation aircraft is also fixed-wing: general-aviation overrides apply after the fixed-wing ones.

phases.description: Flight phases, one group per PirepState (camelCase).

taxiIn.description: Taxi-in (PirepState.TaxiIn): when the aircraft counts as taxiing in after landing.

maxKt.description: Ground speed (kt) below which the aircraft is considered to be taxiing in after landing.

takeoff.description: Takeoff (PirepState.Takeoff): the takeoff roll start, and the helicopter lift-off confirmation.

runwayKt.description: Ground speed (kt) that starts the takeoff roll when the aircraft is on a known runway.

anywhereKt.description: Ground speed (kt) that starts the takeoff roll anywhere, runway known or not.

heliLiftoffSec.description: Helicopter departure: airborne at least this long (s).

heliLiftoffAglFt.description: Helicopter departure: at least this much gain (ft) over the ground baseline.

approach.description: Approach (PirepState.Approach): the sustained descent that moves InitialClimb or Enroute to Approach.

descentFpm.description: Approach consensus: the sustained descent rate (fpm, positive) that moves InitialClimb or Enroute to Approach (mean VS over 5 s at or below minus this). Set per class: light aircraft and helicopters descend slower than jets.

landed.description: Landed (PirepState.Landed): touchdown plausibility and the ground-contact tracker.

touchdownMaxRadioAltFt.description: An on-ground sample with a valid radio altitude above this (ft) and no gear contact is not a touchdown. Rejects building or obstacle strikes the sim reports as ground contact. Unknown radio altitude or gear data always counts as plausible.

contactLandedSec.description: Empirical. Contact held this long (s) means the aircraft is on the ground.

holdSec.description: Touchdown values (rate, g, wheels) become final this long (s) after the contact. Equals the touchdown-g window.

airborneDwellSec.description: Empirical. On-ground false this long (s), with the gain, enters Airborne. Measured from the lift-off edge to the re-contact edge.

airborneGainFt.description: Empirical. Radio-altitude gain (ft) over the ground baseline needed together with the dwell.

airborneGainTimeoutSec.description: On-ground false this long (s) enters Airborne whatever the gain (sloped runway, unusable radio altitude).

sinkRateWindowSec.description: Empirical. Touchdown sink rate is the mean vertical speed over this window (s) ending at the last airborne sample before contact.

oneWheelSec.description: Empirical. One main wheel stable-down this long (s) before the other marks a one-wheel touchdown.

minGainFt.description: Empirical. A span after touchdown that rises at least this much (ft) is a bounce, not a rollout hop.

minAirborneSec.description: Empirical. A span after touchdown airborne at least this long (s) is a bounce, not a rollout hop.

maxSec.description: Empirical. A span this long (s) without a departure is an extended float; the ground held this long closes bounce attribution.

goAround.description: Go-around consensus (EventType.GoAround): the votes that declare a go-around.

climbGainFt.description: Height gained (ft) above the approach low point that declares a go-around.

vsFpm.description: Minimum vertical speed (fpm) during the climb for it to count as a go-around.

climbSeconds.description: Go-around consensus: the window (s) the climbing vote's mean vertical speed is averaged over.

sustainSec.description: Go-around consensus: how long (s) each counted vote must hold true.

fieldCeilingFt.description: Go-around consensus: the episode's low point must be at most this far (ft) above the approach target's elevation, or this high by AGL when no elevation is known.

minGainFt.description: Go-around consensus: the barometric gain (ft) from the low point that is always required.

n1RisePct.description: Go-around consensus: N1 points above the trailing baseline (the lowest N1 over goAround.thrustBaselineSeconds) that cast the thrust vote.

throttleRisePct.description: Go-around consensus: throttle points above the trailing baseline (the lowest throttle over goAround.thrustBaselineSeconds) that cast the thrust vote.

thrustBaselineSeconds.description: Go-around consensus: the trailing window (s, pause-adjusted) whose lowest N1 and throttle are the thrust vote's baseline, so only a fresh advance counts.

circuit.description: Multiple landings: lift-off, roll and stop detection for touch-and-go circuits.

liftoffSeconds.description: Seconds the aircraft must stay airborne after a touchdown for the lift-off to count as a new circuit.

liftoffAglFt.description: AGL (ft) the aircraft must reach after a touchdown for the lift-off to count as a new circuit.

liftoffMinVsFpm.description: Mean vertical speed (fpm) over the circuit.liftoffSeconds window must be at or above this for a lift-off to confirm. Stops a fall off an obstacle (AGL rising while VS is deeply negative) from counting as a departure.

stopKt.description: Ground speed (kt) below which a landing roll is considered stopped, ending the circuit.

rollEnabled.description: Whether a re-acceleration on the runway (a touch-and-go roll) can start a new circuit. Off for helicopters.

rollMinKt.description: Ground speed (kt) floor for a roll attempt. Kept above phases.takeoff.runwayKt so an expedited runway exit after over-slowing does not qualify.

rollAccelKt.description: Ground speed gain (kt) over circuit.rollWindowSeconds that declares a roll attempt.

rollWindowSeconds.description: Sim-clock window (s) over which circuit.rollAccelKt is measured; needs at least three samples, and a gap over two seconds resets it.

rollHeadingToleranceDeg.description: Heading drift (deg) allowed during the roll window for it to still count as a roll on the runway.

departureAfterReverserPenalty.description: Points taken off the landing category (0-100) when the aircraft departs again after reversers were used.

airportLookup.description: Approach candidates: when and how far the background nearby-airport lookup searches.

ceilingAglFt.description: Approach candidates: at or below this AGL (ft) a background nearby-airport lookup may start. Above it a lookup starts only on gear-down or a sustained descent below airportLookup.descentCeilingAglFt.

descentCeilingAglFt.description: Approach candidates: a sustained descent starts a nearby-airport lookup only below this AGL (ft).

rangeNm.description: Approach candidates: the airborne lookup takes the nearest airport with runways within this range (NM).

approachRangeNm.description: Approach candidates: once in the Approach phase, the airborne lookup widens to the 10 nearest airports with runways within this range (NM).

lowFullRateMaxSec.description: Capture policy: full-rate recording below 2,000 ft AGL lasts at most this long (s) per low leg, then drops to 4 Hz.

values.description: A sparse layer of thresholds: any subset of the groups and keys. The full set of values lives in the client; each key's "default" here is that compiled-in value, for reference.
